faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Do I need to install anything?
faq.a1: No. iFan runs in your web browser on any computer or phone. Create an account and you're in — no IT team required.
faq.eq1: Getting started = open your browser and you're in — nothing to install.
faq.q2: Does iFan use personal Zalo or Zalo OA?
faq.a2: iFan uses official Zalo OA only, connected through Zalo’s official API — safe, policy-compliant, never touching personal Zalo accounts. During early access, OA connection is being rolled out gradually to each customer.
faq.eq2: Zalo connection = official Zalo OA only — personal Zalo is never touched.
faq.a3: Each business gets a fully isolated workspace with regular backups. Your customer data belongs to you and is never shared.
faq.eq3: Your customer data = yours alone, fully isolated, never shared.
faq.q4: What if I want to cancel?
faq.a4: Cancel anytime — no contracts, no lock-in. Stop using iFan and you stop paying.
faq.eq4: Canceling = stop using, stop paying — no strings attached.
faq.a5: Yes. The interface ships in Vietnamese and English — switch instantly in-app. More languages are on the roadmap.
faq.eq5: Languages = Vietnamese and English built in — switch instantly in-app.

tinhNang.whyGroupsTitle: Why 9 groups by workflow, not by screen name
tinhNang.whyGroupsDesc: Shop owners don't think in "modules" — they think "customer arrives → close → do the work → collect payment → review." Laid out the way they think, it reads in one pass; laid out by screen name, it becomes a technical catalog.
tinhNang.whyInterleaveTitle: Why unfinished modules sit in the middle, not dumped at the end
tinhNang.whyInterleaveDesc: Dumping them at the end is a kind of hiding — a quick skim would make every group look complete. Placed where they belong, you see right away that "HR & Attendance" has nothing live yet — a truth worth seeing before you sign up.

loTrinh.subtitle: This page is kept in sync with the product's source-of-truth log in the codebase, not written by hand. What's live is marked live; what isn't is marked plainly.

loTrinh.waveV7Extra: internal payroll only — no social-insurance filing, no tax filing
loTrinh.launchTitle: When does it go on sale?
loTrinh.launchDesc: The old bar was “every module on the roadmap shipped” — that bar is now met, 31 of 31 live. What is left is not more modules but maturity: run it alongside a few real shops and fix exactly where they stumble. iFan will not sell a half-finished product and patch it as it goes — so until that part is done, it stays free.
loTrinh.notDoingTitle: Three things iFan deliberately won't do
loTrinh.notDoing1: Full accounting (general ledger, journal entries, tax filings)
loTrinh.notDoing3: An ERP for companies over 100 people
loTrinh.notDoingNote: Said plainly so anyone who needs those doesn't waste time trying iFan.
loTrinh.allDoneDesc: Every module on the map is live. What comes next is not more modules but deeper polish on each one, driven by what shops using it tell us.

footnote.definitions: Revenue counts deals won inside the selected range, with day boundaries in Vietnam time. New customers are counted against the source that first brought them in.
footnote.costNote: Costs are entered per MONTH: the Cost column adds up every month the selected range touches, while the input always edits the current month.
footnote.linearDeals: With the even split, a deal touching several sources is counted under each of them, so the Won deals column can total more than the real number of deals.
footnote.rateOverflow: A source is showing “Customers converted” above 100%: deals won are counted by close date within the range, while new customers are counted by creation date within the range — a customer who arrived earlier but closed inside this range counts as a won deal without counting as a new customer.
footnote.definitionsMore: “Customers converted” = deals won divided by that same source's new customers in the selected range. This is not the “Close rate” on the Overview screen, which is wins over all closed deals. A source with no new customers in the range shows “—” because there is nothing to divide by, even if it still produced revenue from earlier customers.
footnote.profitNote: Profit/Loss = revenue minus ad spend AND minus the cost of goods sold, attributed to the source using the model selected above.
footnote.cogsMissing: Some sources still have order lines with no cost of goods recorded: the cost subtracted is incomplete, so profit on those rows is the HIGHEST it could be (marked “≤”), not the real number. Enter costs for those items on the Products screen and the figures correct themselves.

funnel.subtitle: Six steps, from a stranger landing on a marketing page to finishing shop setup.
funnel.empty: No data for this range yet.
funnel.s1: ① Landed on a marketing page
funnel.byPageNote: “Sign-up clicks” counts clicks on that page only. It does not say which page deserves the credit — someone may read three pages and click on the last one.
funnel.privacyNote: Step ① counts VIEWS, not people: iFan deliberately stores nothing that would recognise a returning visitor — no IP, no device fingerprint, no tracking cookie, nothing sent to a third party. The store holds only date · page · kind · count. Step ⑤ counts only self sign-ups — staff accounts provisioned by a shop owner are excluded. The last two steps read the existing account and shop ledgers, so they are more reliable than the four above, but they can also be larger because they were counting long before the page counter went live.

abtest.title: A/B experiments
abtest.subtitle: Write two versions of the button text on a marketing page; iFan alternates them by day and counts which one gets more sign-up clicks.
abtest.trafficWarning: Plainly: at iFan's current traffic, an experiment needs weeks to months before the numbers mean anything. This screen deliberately refuses to declare a winner until then — a wrong conclusion is worse than none, because it makes you rewrite a page based on a difference that was only luck.
abtest.methodNote: How it alternates: today the whole page uses sentence A, tomorrow sentence B, and so on — visitors are NOT split into two groups, because splitting by person means storing a marker on their device. The trade-off is that weekdays differ (Saturday is not Tuesday), so an experiment must run at least 14 days before a conclusion is allowed, even once it has enough views.
abtest.verdictDone: {ben} wins, with enough data to trust it. The chance this gap is only luck is under 5%. Use this one.

abtest.verdictNeedViews: No conclusion yet — needs about {n} more views on the smaller side.
abtest.verdictTooClose: No conclusion yet. The two sides are too close — this gap is still within the range of luck; a coin toss would produce as much. Let it keep running.

The three fields below are for exceptions the machine cannot know (you let someone leave early that day) — but Recalculate overwrites them, so once you edit by hand, stop recalculating. Days with no roster are skipped for lateness, early leave and overtime rather than guessed.

rates.title: Set rates
